Title: Tuanku Muhriz: Customs cannot be defended by breaching the rules
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Ibni Almarhum Tuanku Munawir today said customs cannot be defended by breaking the very rules of custom, in a pointed address directed at those who have disputed the rules of succession in recent months.
Speaking at Istana Besar Seri Menanti this afternoon to mark the investiture of the 17th Undang of Luak Jelebu, Tuanku Muhriz said Negeri Sembilan’s constitutional monarchy, adat and legal provisions must be upheld together.
“The system of constitutional monarchy in Malaysia... places the Ruler as Head of State. However, His powers are subject to the Constitution and the law, and he serves as an umbrella of unity and a guarantor of the stability of governance,” he said.
“The dignity of the institution of the Ruler must be preserved on the basis of integrity, justice and responsibility.”
In Negeri Sembilan, he said, Adat Perpatih and legal provisions form the basis of the position and succession of the throne. The customary institutions comprising the Undang Yang Empat, Lembaga, Ibu Soko, Buapak and anak buah are an inherited legacy that is vital in safeguarding custom and ensuring the state’s stability.
Disputes must follow custom and law
The Yamtuan further said the customary system must continue to be strengthened to remain relevant with the times, without neglecting its founding principles and rules. Any dispute over the position or succession of the throne, he stressed, must be settled according to the relevant custom and law, not according to personal interests or wishes.
Without naming any party, Tuanku Muhriz said those who in recent months had taken action that gave rise to disputes over the order of succession, on the grounds of defending custom, must understand that custom cannot be defended by violating its own rules.
Such actions, he warned, could damage the standing of the customary and royal institutions, endanger the state’s stability and erode public trust.
The Ruler said the dignity of the monarchy depends on respect for custom, the supremacy of the Constitution and the rule of law. The Ruler’s exalted position, he said, comes with great trust and responsibility, and the people’s confidence is key to ensuring the institution continues to be respected and preserved.
Quoting the Malay proverb “Raja adil raja disembah, raja zalim raja disanggah” (a just ruler is revered; an unjust ruler is opposed), he said justice and integrity must always be the foundation of leadership.
Let history be a guide
Tuanku Muhriz urged Negeri Sembilan citizens to take history as a guide and lesson, and not to let self-interest override truth and justice to the point where security, well-being and a heritage safeguarded across generations are sacrificed.
Custom, he said, is not merely a heritage to be proud of but a trust that must be preserved and defended responsibly.
The future and stability of Negeri Sembilan depend on everyone’s willingness to respect custom, obey the law and place the state’s interests above personal interests for the sake of future generations, he added.

Title: Public Services Commission awaits circular on RM2,500 starting salary for fresh grads entering public service
Article:
KUALA KANGSAR, Oct 14 — The implementation of the RM2,500 starting salary for fresh graduates entering the public service, announced in Budget 2027, is pending an official circular outlining the implementation details.
Malaysian Public Services Commission (SPA) chairman and Judicial and Legal Service Commission (SPKP) chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Jailani Muhamed Yunus said the details would include the implementation timeline and related payment components.
“We welcome the announcement made in the Budget, but its implementation will have to follow the procedures stipulated in the circular.
“More detailed procedures are needed, including how the initiative will be implemented and its timeline,” he told reporters after officiating at the handover of assets under the SPA Madani Adopted School programme at Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan Simpang Beluru here today.
He said preparations for implementing initiatives announced in the budget usually began in the year of the announcement to enable implementation the following year.
Asked whether the RM2,500 amount included other allowances, Ahmad Jailani said the matter would be reviewed and clarified in the official circular.
He said detailed consideration was necessary as the initiative involved a substantial financial allocation and a large number of beneficiaries.
“This matter must be handled carefully and systematically. I am confident that the relevant parties have done their work and that the matter can be resolved satisfactorily,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia gives Nepal US$1m in flood relief aid
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 14 — Malaysia has handed over US$1 million (RM4.08 million) in humanitarian assistance to Nepal to support relief and recovery efforts following devastating floods that struck the country on August 26.
Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan presented the contribution to Nepal’s Chargé d’Affaires in Kuala Lumpur, Mudita Bajracharya, at a ceremony here on Wednesday, according to the Foreign Ministry, also known as Wisma Putra.
“The contribution reflects Malaysia’s unwavering support for the government and people of Nepal during this difficult time,” Wisma Putra said in a statement.
Mohamad also conveyed Malaysia’s deepest sympathies and heartfelt condolences to the government and people of Nepal, particularly to the families who lost their loved ones and all those affected by the disaster, it said.
Wisma Putra said Mohamad welcomed the Nepalese government's approval of a new ordinance concerning the declaration of death of victims who remain uncontactable, which reduces the applicable period from 12 years to 45 days from the date of the disaster.
“The new ordinance will provide greater legal and administrative certainty for affected families,” Wisma Putra said.
The ministry said Nepal’s Chargé d’Affaires in Kuala Lumpur conveyed that the details of the ordinance and its modalities were being finalised by the government of Nepal.
“Malaysia stands in solidarity with the government and people of Nepal throughout the recovery and reconstruction process and reaffirms its support for international humanitarian efforts in the aftermath of the disaster,” the ministry said. — Bernama

Title: Haze: Schools in Selangor, Negeri Sembilan, Melaka, Pahang to reopen tomorrow
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — Educational institutions under the Ministry of Education (MOE) in Selangor, Negeri Sembilan, Melaka and Pahang will reopen tomorrow.
The Selangor State Education Department said school operations in the state will prioritise the safety, health and well-being of pupils and school staff.
“Pupils are encouraged to wear face masks as a precaution. Parents or guardians who are concerned about their children’s health amid the haze may choose not to send them to school.
“However, they must notify the school if their children will be absent,” it said in a statement today.
In Negeri Sembilan, the state Education Department reminded schools to monitor air quality regularly, comply with the guidelines in force and take appropriate measures to safeguard pupils’ health.
“Schools must suspend all outdoor activities, including Physical Education lessons, co-curricular activities, sports, camping, celebrations, assemblies and activities in open halls, when the Air Pollutant Index (API) reading exceeds 100,” the department said.
The Melaka State Education Department said educational institutions under MOE will resume operations tomorrow, pending official confirmation of the latest API readings.
The department urged administrators to take appropriate measures to ensure smooth operations and comply with the ministry’s directives, while immediately suspending all outdoor activities and assemblies.
“Students are encouraged to wear face masks and drink water regularly. Parents and guardians are advised to continue monitoring their children’s health and seek medical attention if they develop symptoms related to air pollution.
“Any changes to the operating instructions will be announced on the official Melaka State Education Department Facebook page,” the statement said.
Schools in Pekan, Kuantan, Rompin, Temerloh, Maran, Bera and Bentong in Pahang will also reopen tomorrow, the State Education Department said.
Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek yesterday announced the closure of all schools in Johor, Melaka and Negeri Sembilan, as well as several districts in Selangor, Pahang, Sabah and Sarawak, today due to haze. — Bernama

Title: Parliament’s new service council to be fully operational by December, says Dewan Rakyat Speaker
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — The Parliamentary Service Council (MPP), which will oversee the administrative autonomy of the Malaysian Parliament, is expected to be fully operational by December.
Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul said the council would oversee matters including the service scheme, career paths and administration of parliamentary officers, as well as ensure compliance with the provisions of the Parliamentary Services Act 2025.
“We hope the establishment of the MPP, beginning in December, will enable Parliament to restore the principle of separation of powers and strengthen the country’s democracy in accordance with the mandate of the Federal Constitution,” he told a press conference after the handover ceremony marking administrative transition and institutional reform at the Malaysian Parliament here today.
The event was attended by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, Dewan Negara President Senator Datuk Seri Awang Bemee Awang Ali Basah, Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar and Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said.
Johari said the establishment of the MPP followed the official enforcement of the Parliamentary Services Act 2025 on October 1, restoring Parliament’s administrative independence after 33 years under the Prime Minister’s Department (JPM).
He said the MPP would be co-chaired by the Dewan Rakyat Speaker and the Dewan Negara President, with a total membership of 16.
Johari said its members would include the Director-General of Public Services (KPPA), Treasury Secretary-General (KSP), four Members of Parliament and two senators, who would be elected when the Dewan Negara sitting begins on Nov 30.
At the Dewan Rakyat sitting this morning, the prime minister tabled a motion to appoint four MPs to the MPP, which was passed by a majority without debate.
The four appointees, comprising two government and two opposition representatives, are Ramkarpal Singh (PH-Bukit Gelugor), Datuk Seri Hasni Mohammad (BN-Simpang Renggam), Datuk Seri Dr Ronald Kiandee (PN-Beluran) and Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan (PN-Kota Bharu). — Bernama

Title: Weather warning: MetMalaysia puts most of the country on thunderstorm alert
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued an afternoon thunderstorm advisory, warning that heavy downpours, gusty winds, and lightning will lash widespread areas across Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah, and Sarawak until 7pm today.
The advisory places the entirety of Perlis, Penang, Kuala Lumpur, and Putrajaya on alert, alongside large swathes of the northern and central peninsula.
In Kedah, stormy weather is forecast for Kubang Pasu, Padang Terap, Sik, Baling, Kulim, and Bandar Baharu. Perak faces widespread disruption across Kerian, Selama, Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Larut Matang, Kinta, Kampar, Batang Padang, Muallim, and Bagan Datuk.
Across Selangor, the warning blankets Sabak Bernam, Kuala Selangor, Hulu Selangor, Gombak, Petaling, Hulu Langat, and Sepang. Further south, the alert covers Jempol in Negeri Sembilan and Segamat in Johor.
East coast states are similarly braced for severe weather. Kelantan will see storms hit Tanah Merah, Kuala Krai, Machang, Pasir Mas, Tumpat, Kota Bharu, Pasir Puteh, and Bachok. In Terengganu, bad weather is expected across Hulu Terengganu, Besut, Dungun, Kemaman, and Setiu, while Pahang residents in Kuantan, Maran, Jerantut, Bera, and Rompin have also been advised to brace for rain.
Across East Malaysia, the warning stretches across multiple divisions in Sarawak. These include Kuching, Serian and Siburan, Samarahan, Sri Aman, Betong, Sarikei (incorporating Julau), Sibu, Mukah (covering Daro, Matu, and Dalat), Kapit (including Song), Miri (featuring Marudi and Beluru), and Limbang.
In Sabah, the alert spans the interior divisions of Sipitang, Beaufort, Membakut, and Tambunan, before extending across the West Coast through Papar, Penampang, Kota Kinabalu, Tuaran, and Kota Belud. Other affected areas in the state include Kota Marudu in Kudat, Kinabatangan in Sandakan, and Kunak in Tawau.
MetMalaysia issues thunderstorm warnings whenever rain clouds show signs of dumping more than 20mm of rain per hour, or when high-intensity downpours are imminent and likely to persist beyond an hour.
The department noted that these warnings serve as short-term alerts, with each issuance remaining valid for a maximum of six hours.

Title: Nhaveen murder trial: Prosecution cites contradictions in four accused’s defence
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Oct 14 — The High Court here was told today that there are four main grounds for the prosecution’s bid to convict the four accused in the murder of teenager T. Nhaveen nine years ago, with the contention that the defence failed to raise reasonable doubt against its case.
Deputy Public Prosecutor (DPP) Mohd Amril Johari said among these grounds was the contradiction between the defence’s version during the prosecution’s case and the accused’s testimony at the defence stage last week.
He said the defence of all four accused had shifted when they gave evidence themselves, particularly regarding a claim by one of them, who was a teenager at the time of the incident, that he was beaten unconscious with a helmet by Nhaveen’s friend, T. Previin, while trying to break up a fight.
Mohd Amril described the claim as an afterthought, as it had not been raised earlier, and said the contradictions in the accused’s testimony raised questions over the defence’s credibility.
“The defence’s case at the prosecution stage is totally different from the defence now. So, they are shifting the goalposts.
“The prosecution’s theory also does not dispute their (the accused’s) presence at both locations — Jalan Kaki Bukit and Padang Openg, Gelugor,” he said while submitting during the defence proceedings of the four individuals charged with Nhaveen’s murder.
He questioned the absence of a medical report to support the accused’s claim of being injured to the point of losing consciousness.
He also noted that the issue of a phone call made by one of the accused, J. Ragesuthen, 27, to Nhaveen’s mother, T. Shanti, on the night of the incident was supported by witness testimony.
Mohd Amril asked the court to examine the difference between the brief grounds of judgment of the Court of Appeal, which ordered the four accused to enter their defence, and the full grounds of judgment in the appeal involving another respondent, S. Gopinaath, 35, who was acquitted and discharged.
However, lawyer Maanveer Singh Dhillon, representing all four accused, argued that reasonable doubt remains over how and where the injuries that led to Nhaveen’s death occurred.
He said Nhaveen was still alive after the incident at Jalan Kaki Bukit and had ridden a motorcycle with an individual known as “Belang,” but what happened afterwards could not be ascertained based on the evidence presented in court.
He said the testimony of prosecution witnesses and medical evidence must be assessed as a whole, including the question of whether the injuries Nhaveen sustained occurred at the scene of the fight or after he was taken away.
Maanveer Singh also questioned the discrepancy in the number of individuals said to have been involved in the incident based on several versions of testimony, and stressed that the defence did not deny a scuffle had taken place at Jalan Kaki Bukit, but disputed whether that incident caused Nhaveen’s death.
Judge Datuk Mohd Radzi Abdul Hamid then set November 16 for case management to allow the prosecution and defence to file additional submissions before a decision date is fixed.
The four accused, Ragesuthan, S. Gokulan, 27, and two others who were teenagers at the time of the incident, gave their witness statements on October 8 and 9 last year.
They were charged under Section 302 of the Penal Code for Nhaveen’s murder, which carries the death penalty or imprisonment of 30 to 40 years and not less than 12 strokes of the cane, upon conviction.
They were also charged under Section 326 of the same law for voluntarily causing grievous hurt to Previin with dangerous weapons, which provides for up to 20 years’ imprisonment and a fine or caning.
Nhaveen and Previin were 18 and 19 years old, respectively, at the time of the incident.
In addition to Mohd Amril, DPPs Yazid Mustaqim Roslan and Noor Azura Zulkiflee also appeared for the prosecution, while all four accused are represented by lawyers Maanveer Singh, R. Thevan and Lim Sheng Zhe. Lawyer T. Gunaseelan is holding a watching brief for Nhaveen’s family.
Previously, the Court of Appeal ordered Ragesuthan, Gokulan and the two teenagers to enter their defence on the charge of murdering Nhaveen after allowing the prosecution’s appeal against the High Court decision that acquitted them on October 3, 2023.
They were also ordered to enter their defence on the charge of injuring Previin near the Karpal Singh Learning Centre at Jalan Kaki Bukit, Gelugor, between 11pm and midnight on June 9, 2017.
Nhaveen died on June 15, 2017, after six days of treatment at Penang Hospital from severe injuries sustained in the incident. — Bernama

Title: Five govt buildings get solar installations ahead of schedule, says works minister
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 14 — Five grid-connected photovoltaic (GCPV) solar installation projects at government buildings have been completed ahead of schedule, with a combined installed capacity of 779.86 kilowatts, Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi said.
He said two of the projects were at Ministry of Foreign Affairs premises, while the other three were at the National Water Research Institute of Malaysia (Nahrim), Hospital Canselor Tuanku Muhriz (HCTM) and the Department of Irrigation and Drainage (DID).
“This is a concrete step towards expanding the use of clean energy at government premises, while reducing operating costs and supporting more sustainable public asset management,” he said at a ceremony to hand over the projects to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and three other government premises here today.
He said the Public Works Department (JKR) had also implemented grid-connected photovoltaic and off-grid solar installations involving 46 Federal Government buildings, 283 rural schools in Sabah, Sarawak and Peninsular Malaysia, four Royal Malaysia Police border posts and an Orang Asli village.
“These projects have the potential to generate energy cost savings of up to RM115 million annually compared with conventional electricity supplies,” he said.
Nanta said the government-building solar installation programme, led by the Ministry of Economy, received an allocation of RM57.6 million, with an initial target of installing nine megawatts of capacity in Peninsular Malaysia.
As of last September, eight projects involving 23 buildings with a capacity of 5.8 megawatts had completed their Defects Liability Period (DLP), while seven projects involving 11 buildings with a capacity of 2.09 megawatts remained within the period.
He said three other projects involving 11 buildings with a capacity of 1.29 megawatts were under construction, while another project involving one building, with a capacity of 0.5 megawatts, was at the procurement stage.
“When all the systems are fully operational, the programme is projected to generate about 13,200 megawatt-hours of electricity annually, with potential gross savings of around RM5.5 million a year on government electricity bills,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Why should a good man go when the corrupt stay? Anwar says Malaysia needs ministers like Anthony Loke
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 14 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim sought again today to make a case for Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook to remain in his Cabinet, saying the country needs principled leaders and that the corrupt should be the ones stepping down.
Speaking at the Transport Ministry during the distribution of RM1,000 special financial assistance to taxi, rental car, and school bus drivers, Anwar commended Loke's dedication to ordinary working Malaysians, including the initiative today.
“Some people think people like him should step down. Why should a good person like him have to resign? The ones who should resign are those involved in corruption,” he said in his speech.
“I told him to stay on and get the job done, because the country needs principled leaders. This country needs leaders who care about ordinary people,” he said, noting that leaders must stay focused on the daily struggles of fishermen, farmers, and low-wage workers.
Loke, who is the DAP secretary-general, tendered his resignation as transport minister on September 19 following the political controversy surrounding the conditional royal pardon granted to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak.
Loke subsequently clarified on September 29 that he would continue serving until the issue of Najib's proposed house arrest is resolved.
Record plate sales fund driver aid
Today’s ceremony marked the immediate rollout of the RM1,000 one-off grant announced under Budget 2027 last Friday. The initiative is funded entirely by revenue generated from the Transport Ministry's special 'H' vehicle registration series, which netted RM91.2 million, far eclipsing initial projections of RM30 million.
The series set a national record for the most expensive vehicle registration number in Malaysian history, with H1 selling for RM10 million.
“The car is not included; it is just the number plate,” Loke said, in apparent jest. “This is the highest amount ever paid for a single vehicle registration number in our country.”
Loke explained that he proposed channelling the auction proceeds to public transport drivers during a working trip to Sarawak.
“I knew the prime minister had a soft spot for taxi drivers. When I made the proposal, he said, ‘Good idea, go ahead’,” Loke said.
Around 500 drivers received the RM1,000 aid vouchers at today's event to help offset operating overheads and vehicle maintenance.
The ministry will expand distribution nationwide in phases, beginning in Penang on October 17, with early disbursements timed to assist Hindu drivers ahead of the upcoming Deepavali festival.

Title: Sarawak Education Dept: Schools open tomorrow, outdoor activities halted if API tops 100
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 14 — All schools and educational institutions under the Ministry of Education (MOE) in Sarawak will operate as usual tomorrow, despite the ongoing haze affecting several areas in the state.
In a statement today, the Sarawak Education Department (JPN) said schools in areas where the Air Pollutant Index (API) reading exceeded 100 must suspend all outdoor activities.
“Students attending school are encouraged to wear face masks as a precautionary measure amid the current haze situation.
“Parents and guardians may choose not to send their children to school if they have concerns about their health due to the haze affecting several locations in Sarawak, provided they inform the school,” the statement said.
Yesterday, the department announced the temporary closure of all primary and secondary schools under the Serian, Sri Aman and Lubok Antu District Education Offices (PPD), with Teaching and Learning at Home (PdPR) implemented during the closure. — Bernama

Title: MACC: Fighting corruption starts with rejecting bribes, reporting misconduct
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — Integrity must show up in everyday actions, including rejecting bribes, complying with regulations, and having the courage to report misconduct, so society shares responsibility in the fight against corruption.
Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Deputy Chief Commissioner (Prevention) Datuk Azmi Kamaruzaman said building a corruption-free culture starts with honest decisions and firm personal convictions, supported by sustained commitment from all parties.
“We can progress when there is no abuse of power. The shift towards a corruption-free culture begins with our own honest decisions and firm convictions,” he said.
He was speaking at the launch of the “Program Langkah Merdeka 118, Bersama Perangi Rasuah” programme, held in conjunction with the MACC’s 59th anniversary celebration for Kuala Lumpur at Stadium Merdeka here today. The programme was organised in collaboration with Permodalan Nasional Berhad (PNB) Merdeka Ventures.
Azmi said the corruption-free pledge taken by PNB Merdeka Ventures at the event should not be merely a declaration on paper, but must serve as the foundation for a clean, transparent and ethical workplace, thereby safeguarding public trust in the organisation.
Meanwhile, Kuala Lumpur MACC director Mohamad Zakkuan Talib said the symbolic act of carrying and hoisting the MACC flag atop Merdeka 118, Malaysia’s tallest building and the world’s second tallest, reflected the commission’s determination to elevate the anti-corruption agenda and strengthen integrity without compromise.
The programme also featured a tower run involving Kuala Lumpur City Hall, the Royal Malaysia Police, the Fire and Rescue Department of Malaysia, Tenaga Nasional Berhad, the Construction Industry Development Board Malaysia and MACC officers.
Lance Corporal Muhamad Khairul Izwan Mazli from the Cheras District Police Headquarters emerged champion with a time of 32 minutes and 29 seconds, while Wan Norrazif Mohameed from the Kuala Lumpur MACC office finished second, followed by Mohd Hanief Afiq Rosnei from the Negeri Sembilan MACC office in third place.
An integrity exhibition featuring nearly 20 government and private-sector ministries and agencies was also held, with participation from the Health Ministry, Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry, Malaysian Institute of Integrity, National Anti-Drugs Agency and Dewan Bahasa dan Pustaka, among others.
Various services were offered, including health and dental screenings, account checks with the Employees Provident Fund (EPF) and the National Higher Education Fund Corporation (PTPTN), as well as Rahmah Sales, book sales and jewellery sales. — Bernama

Title: Paddy farmers who suffered yield losses from fertiliser delays may get targeted aid, says minister
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — The government will assess whether to provide targeted assistance to paddy farmers whose yields declined due to delays in fertiliser supplies, evaluating affected cases on a case-by-case basis.
Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu said the assessment would identify farmers who genuinely suffered losses before considering any assistance.
“We will study and discuss the issue of losses so that, if funds are available, assistance can be channelled in a targeted manner rather than universally. We are looking at those who experienced yield declines and will assess the situation on a case-by-case basis in affected areas,” he said during the question-and-answer session in the Dewan Rakyat today.
He was responding to a supplementary question from Sabri Azit (PN-Jerai) on the possibility of providing incentives to padi affected by delays in fertiliser supplies.
Mohamad said he had taken proactive steps by meeting the management of the Muda Agricultural Development Authority (Mada) to seek an explanation for the delays.
He added that he had also obtained information from the relevant officials before proposing to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who is also Finance Minister, that the services of suppliers who failed to fulfil their obligations be terminated.
In a separate development, Deputy Defence Minister Adly Zahari said 10 per cent of the funds collected through the Warriors’ Fund Campaign (KTP) had been allocated for investment in fixed deposits with financial institutions.
He said the strategy was aimed at generating returns to grow the fund and support assistance and welfare programmes for veterans and their dependants in need.
“As of September 22, RM1.51 million had been placed in a fixed deposit with Bank Islam Malaysia Bhd at a profit rate of 3.6 per cent, maturing on March 15, 2027.
“In addition, KTP has received an allocation of RM2 million from the Finance Ministry, and approval is pending to place the funds in a new fixed deposit to generate additional returns,” he said.
Adly was responding to a question from Nordin Ahmad Ismail (PN-Lumut) on the strategic direction of the Warriors’ Fund (Tabung Pahlawan) transformation, particularly efforts to move away from reliance on seasonal public contributions towards a sustainable fundraising model driven by strategic investments or corporate partnerships. — Bernama

Title: Foreign minister: Malaysians in Riyadh, Jeddah safe amid Saudi tensions
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 14 — Malaysians living and working in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, have been reported safe amid continuing tensions in the country, Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said.
He said daily reports from the Malaysian Embassy in Riyadh and the Malaysian Consulate in Jeddah confirmed that Malaysians in both cities were safe and well.
“I receive daily reports from our embassy in Riyadh and our consul in Jeddah confirming that Malaysians there are all right.
“The Malaysian workers there are also safe,” he told reporters after attending the handover ceremony for a solar photovoltaic (grid-connected PV) system installation project by the Works Ministry to the Foreign Ministry and three other government premises here today.
Mohamad said the embassy and consulate remained in contact with Malaysians in the respective cities to monitor their safety and well-being.
He also advised Malaysians in Saudi Arabia to stay away from public areas and strategic locations that could potentially be targeted in attacks.
“As far as possible, they should remain at home. We are also using the e-Konsular system to maintain contact with them,” he said.
Mohamad said several Malaysians in Jeddah had also been temporarily stranded following the cancellation of return flights amid operational disruptions affecting Malaysian and international airlines.
He said the security situation in Saudi Arabia remained tense following another reported attack yesterday.
The attack was reported to have targeted an Aramco complex belonging to the Saudi Arabian oil company, which operates large-scale oil refining and production facilities.
In view of the situation, Mohamad advised Malaysians without urgent reasons to travel to Saudi Arabia to postpone their trips until the security situation improved.
In a separate development, he said the ministry could provide consular assistance to Malaysians detained in Japan in connection with drug-related cases, but legal proceedings fell under the jurisdiction of the Japanese authorities.
He said Japan maintained strict confidentiality to protect the privacy of detainees, and consular visits could not be arranged without their consent.
“We cannot simply arrange a visit at the request of family members without the consent of the person detained.
“If the family wants us to conduct a consular visit to check on the detainee’s welfare or provide any necessary assistance, they should ask the detainee or the person concerned to submit a written request to the Japanese authorities,” he said.
It was reported that four Malaysian men and a woman had been detained at Haneda Airport in Tokyo last Saturday for allegedly attempting to smuggle about five kilogrammes of cocaine worth ¥120 million (RM3.1 million), concealed beneath shoe insoles.
The group was believed to have transported the drugs from Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) in Sepang before being discovered during customs checks upon arrival in Japan. — Bernama

Title: Johor JPJ seeks p-hailing operators’ help to curb repeat offences, especially running red lights
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 14 — The Johor Road Transport Department (JPJ) will meet p-hailing operators to discuss measures to raise riders’ awareness of road safety and curb repeat traffic offences, particularly running red lights.
State JPJ director Zulkarnain Yasin said the department had received numerous complaints about traffic offences involving p-hailing riders, particularly running red lights, captured in dashboard camera footage.
According to him, operators should play a role in developing appropriate mechanisms to raise riders’ awareness, remind them not to repeat offences and prevent accidents.
“Through the meeting, I want to find out whether operators have policies to prevent, restrict or suspend riders from operating,” he said in an interview with Bernama here today.
He said JPJ also imposed demerit points on road users who repeatedly committed offences such as running red lights, in addition to issuing summonses.
Zulkarnain said operators also needed to take proactive measures, adding that responsibility should not rest entirely with the authorities.
“Those who run red lights will be given demerit points. Once they accumulate 20 points, their driving licences will certainly be suspended.
“That is one of the measures we take, but we want to know whether p-hailing operators have their own methods that could help us,” he said.
According to him, road accident records and studies showed that motorcyclists accounted for between 60 and 70 per cent of accidents and fatalities.
He said the department continued to strengthen enforcement, particularly in accident-prone areas, as part of its key performance indicators (KPIs) to reduce road accidents.
JPJ was also obtaining the latest statistics on accidents involving p-hailing riders from the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) in conjunction with the planned meeting, he added. — Bernama

Title: Budget 2027: Tengku Zafrul urges local semiconductor firms to move up value chain
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — Local semiconductor companies must translate Budget 2027’s allocation into greater participation in higher-value activities such as integrated circuit (IC) design, as Malaysia seeks to strengthen its position in the global semiconductor supply chain, said Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Abdul Aziz.
Speaking on Bernama TV’s
The Nation
programme, the Malaysian Investment Development Authority (Mida) chairman said Malaysia has developed a mature semiconductor ecosystem over more than five decades but needs to move beyond its traditional strengths in assembly and testing to capture greater value from the industry.
“We have Malaysian companies that are already global champions and they are plugged into the global value chain, but we need to see more. The ecosystem is quite mature but we need to strengthen the way we are in that value chain,” he said in the interview on Budget 2027 aired today.
Under Budget 2027, Khazanah Nasional Bhd and the Kumpulan Wang Persaraan (Diperbadankan) (KWAP) will invest RM1.2 billion to support local semiconductor companies in moving into higher-value segments of the industry.
The Budget also provides for a RM100 million Strategic Investment Fund to be established by Khazanah Nasional Bhd and InvestPenang to support early-stage semiconductor and advanced manufacturing companies.
Tengku Zafrul said the measures would help Malaysian companies strengthen their capabilities and move further up the value chain.
He said investments should generate wider economic spillovers by strengthening local supply chains and creating opportunities for domestic businesses.
“If we move up this value chain, we need to make sure that Malaysia really looks at opportunities (such as) how we can then invest more in research and development (R&D) and innovation,” he said.
At the same time, Tengku Zafrul said, the government must focus not only on attracting investments but also on ensuring that approved projects are realised within a reasonable timeframe.
He said the process of securing approvals from local councils and relevant government agencies remain an important consideration for investors, with the speed of implementation varying across sectors.
“Investment projects, particularly in manufacturing, could take about two years from groundbreaking to the completion of factories, depending on the industry,” he noted.
On wages, he opined that companies should translate productivity gains into higher wages for employees to ensure that economic growth delivers better livelihoods for Malaysians.
“I’m definitely a proponent of ensuring that wages must increase in line with productivity,” he said, adding that companies that recorded higher profits through improved efficiency and productivity should share those gains with their employees. — Bernama

Title: 1MDB trial: Judge rejects Najib’s bid to stay prison sentence, says his medical issues not special circumstances
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — The High Court today dismissed former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s application to stay the execution of his 15-year prison sentence and RM11.38 billion fine in the 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB) corruption case.
The decision clears the way for a fresh warrant of committal to be executed against Najib once he completes his reduced custodial sentence in the SRC International Sdn Bhd case, with his 15-year 1MDB jail term scheduled to commence in August 2028.
Delivering her decision, High Court Judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin held that the gravity of the offences and overarching public interest considerations outweighed the applicant's private grievances.
She further rejected lawyers’ assertions that Najib's health constituted a special circumstance warranting a stay.
“Having weighed the competing interests of the applicant against public interest considerations, the court does not agree that the medical issues raised satisfy the special circumstances test,” the judge said.
“The medical report gave me the impression that the applicant’s medical needs are very well taken care of by the government, hospitals and experts.”
Noor Ruwena also ruled that the multi-billion-ringgit fine did not amount to special circumstances, as payment is not enforceable until his avenues for appeal are exhausted.
“Therefore, I find no merit in this application and it is accordingly dismissed,” she said.
Arguing against the stay, Deputy Public Prosecutor Datuk Ahmad Akram Gharib submitted that granting interim relief would inflict tangible prejudice on the public interest and undermine judicial finality in a trial spanning seven years.
“On the balance of convenience, the applicant’s grievance is speculative and the public’s interest in the enforcement of a valid conviction is real and immediate,” Akram argued.
“We submit that the applicant has failed to discharge the burden — which rests squarely upon him — of establishing the existence of special or exceptional circumstances warranting the extraordinary exercise of the court’s discretion.
“The interests of justice, the gravity of the offences, the accused’s prior convictions and the overwhelming public interest considerations all compel the conclusion that the application ought to be dismissed,” he added.
Lead defence counsel Tan Sri Muhammad Shafee Abdullah explained that the stay was not filed immediately after the verdict on Dec 26 last year to preserve Najib's eligibility for concurrent sentencing should his appeal succeed:
“The non-application for a stay on that day was expressly premised upon the applicant’s liberty to apply for a stay at a later date, depending on subsequent developments in the law or other circumstances,” he said.
Najib was convicted on Dec 26 last year by then-trial judge Datuk Collin Lawrence Sequerah, now a Federal Court judge, on four counts of abuse of power and 21 counts of money laundering involving RM2.3 billion in 1MDB funds, carrying a 15-year jail term, an RM11.38 billion fine, and a recoverable sum of RM2.081 billion.
Najib is already in prison, serving his sentence stemming from a separate conviction in the SRC International trial.
On Sept 18, Federal Territories Pardons Board announced that Najib could serve the remainder of his reduced SRC sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028, subject to conditions including payment of a RM50 million fine.

Title: Damansara mini tornado caused by active thunderstorm clouds, says MetMalaysia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — The mini tornado or landspout that struck Damansara, Selangor, yesterday evening was caused by active thunderstorm clouds (cumulonimbus), said Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) director-general Dr Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip.
He said a tornado is a fast-rotating column of air, formed by the presence of wind shear and updrafts during the development of thunderstorm clouds.
Mohd Hisham said tornadoes in Malaysia occur only on a relatively small scale, measuring less than 10 metres and lasting for a very short time.
“This makes their formation difficult to detect by radar and weather satellites, but MetMalaysia had issued a thunderstorm warning for districts in Selangor at 5.30pm on October 13,” he told Bernama today.
Mohd Hisham said landspouts, tornadoes over land and waterspouts over the sea occur frequently during the monsoon transition phase, from March to May and September to October.
He said the phenomenon is caused by unstable, humid atmospheric conditions, along with weak winds blowing from multiple directions.
Yesterday, social media users shared several videos showing the tornado as vehicles were stopped at a toll plaza, with strong winds appearing to lift the rear end of a vehicle off the ground. — Bernama

Title: Man drives SUV 130m down train tracks in Port Klang, police say KTMB investigating
Article:
KLANG, Oct 14 — A 60-year-old motorist drove his SUV onto railway tracks and travelled roughly 130 metres before coming to a stop at a KTMB station in Pelabuhan Klang, police confirmed today.
The late-night incident occurred around 11.40pm on Oct 11 at a level crossing near the Jalan Limbungan KTMB station, Klang South district police chief ACP Lim Jit Huey said in a statement today.
“According to preliminary police investigations, the driver, a Kuala Lumpur resident, was heading home when his vehicle strayed onto the tracks,” Lim said.
Instead of backing away, the man drove along the railway corridor for about 130 metres until pulling up directly at the Jalan Limbungan platform in Pelabuhan Klang, Selangor.
Railway operator Keretapi Tanah Melayu Bhd (KTMB) then moved to clear the SUV from the line, finally removing the vehicle at 1.40am.
Lim confirmed that KTMB has taken the lead in the probe, investigating the case under Section 62 of the Railways Act 1991, which addresses trespassing on railway land.
Police did not disclose how or why the driver ended up on the tracks, and authorities reported no injuries, vehicle wreckage, or structural damage along the rail line.
Earlier, videos of the incident were shared online.

Title: King attends 273rd Conference of Rulers at Istana Negara
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, today attended the 273rd Conference of Rulers meeting at Istana Negara, chaired by the Sultan of Perak, Sultan Nazrin Shah.
Present were the Raja of Perlis, Tuanku Syed Sirajuddin Jamalullail; Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah; Sultan of Kedah, Al-Aminul Karim Sultan Sallehuddin Sultan Badlishah; and Sultan of Pahang, Al-Sultan Abdullah Ri’ayatuddin Al-Mustafa Billah Shah.
The Regent of Terengganu, Tengku Muhammad Ismail; Crown Prince of Kelantan, Tengku Muhammad Fakhry Petra; and Tunku Temenggong of Johor, Tunku Idris Iskandar Sultan Ibrahim, also attended.
The meeting was also attended by the four Governors, namely Tun Dr Mohd Ali Rustam of Melaka, Tun Dr Wan Junaidi Tuanku Jaafar of Sarawak, Tun Musa Aman of Sabah and Tun Ramli Ngah Talib of Penang.
The rulers were accompanied by their respective Menteri Besar and Chief Ministers. Deputy Premier of Sarawak was also present.
The previous Conference of Rulers meeting was held on Feb 11 and 12, chaired by the Sultan of Terengganu, Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin. — Bernama

Title: Anwar hails Parliamentary Services Act as key reform
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim described the implementation of the Parliamentary Services Act 2025 as a key step by the MADANI Government towards fulfilling its reform pledge to the people, including limiting powers traditionally held by the government.
He said the move was a key pillar of the country’s reform agenda, reflecting the government’s commitment to strengthening Parliament’s independence and advancing the maturity of the country’s parliamentary democracy.
“I consider this change and the Parliamentary Services Act important because they give meaning to parliamentary democracy and reflect the maturity of our democratic system.
“This is one of the important steps that I regard as a cornerstone of the MADANI Government’s reform agenda – fulfilling our promise to the people by introducing and passing the Parliamentary Services Act to limit powers traditionally held by the government,” he said.
Anwar was speaking at the Malaysian Parliament’s Administrative Transition and Institutional Reform ceremony, held at the Parliament Building here today in conjunction with the implementation of the Parliamentary Services Act 2025.
Also present were Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul, Dewan Negara President Senator Datuk Seri Awang Bemee Awang Ali Basah and Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar.
Recounting the history of parliamentary administration, Anwar said efforts to strengthen Parliament’s independence had been a long process, dating back to the introduction of relevant legislation in the 1960s before it was repealed in 1992.
He said the reinstatement of the Parliamentary Services Act reflected the commitment to further advancing parliamentary democracy, with its success also depending on the credibility of the leadership of both houses and the willingness of MPs to support the reform.
Anwar also expressed hope that the independence and new powers granted to Parliament would be used to strengthen the capabilities and professionalism of its staff, while improving the quality and decorum of parliamentary debates.
“With Parliament now having the independence and authority to develop the capabilities of its own staff and enhance their professionalism, we also hope to see improvements in the quality of debates and the decorum of proceedings, in keeping with its new powers.
“This requires the cooperation of all parties, including members of the government administration, government MPs and opposition MPs. The independence granted must be exercised with an understanding of the limits and responsibilities inherent in a democratic system,” he said.
At the Dewan Rakyat sitting this morning, a motion tabled by Anwar to appoint four MPs to the Selection Committee under the Parliamentary Services Act 2025 was passed by a majority vote.
The four MPs, comprising two government representatives and two from the opposition, are Ramkarpal Singh (PH-Bukit Gelugor), Datuk Seri Hasni Mohammad (BN-Simpang Renggam), Datuk Seri Dr Ronald Kiandee (PN-Beluran) and Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan (PN-Kota Bharu). — Bernama

Title: MPS urges Putrajaya to detail contract pharmacists’ absorption timeline and quota numbers
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — The Malaysian Pharmacists Society (MPS) has welcomed the government’s move to recommend contract pharmacy officers for permanent posts, but insists Putrajaya must quickly settle the critical details on quota figures, eligibility rules, and an implementation timeline.
The response follows remarks by Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad, who confirmed on Monday that the Ministry of Health (MOH) will submit a proposal to the Ministry of Finance and the Cabinet to absorb contract pharmacy officers into permanent positions.
He said permanent posts for dental and pharmacy personnel will come from a distinct allocation, separate from the 9,000 permanent medical officer positions unveiled under Budget 2027.
In a statement today, MPS singled out this dedicated quota and the pledge of a reasonable timeframe as encouraging signals for thousands of young officers who continue to staff public hospitals and clinics amid persistent career uncertainty.
Figures from the society show that 3,545 contract pharmacists remained on MOH rosters as of July 2026, while another 115 sat on the reserve list or awaited formal appointment.
“The latest clarification provides an important indication of the Government’s policy direction,” MPS president Prof Ph. Amrahi Buang said in the statement.
“The priority now is to translate this commitment into a clear, transparent and implementable pathway.”
To turn this commitment into reality, the society is seeking urgent clarification on the exact number of permanent positions to be created and when the proposal will reach the Cabinet and the Treasury.
It also wants transparent criteria detailing which cohorts will qualify, whether the 115 candidates on reserve will receive priority placement, and what options remain for those who have already exhausted their contract tenure but still wish to serve in the public healthcare system.
The society also urged authorities to reveal how evaluation panels will weigh clinical experience, seniority, and local staffing needs during the selection process, including whether appointments will be phased.
While MPS acknowledged that opening permanent posts demands seamless coordination between MOH, the Public Services Department, and the Treasury, it warned that prolonged ambiguity risks driving talent out of the public sector.
Beyond immediate absorption, the society also called on Putrajaya to weave these measures into a long-term pharmacy workforce strategy that reflects evolving clinical roles, frontline workload, and talent retention.
MPS pledged to work closely with MOH and central agencies through its Public Pharmacists Chapter, urging regular public updates as the Cabinet paper takes shape.
Contract dentistry faces a parallel challenge. The Malaysian Dental Association recently pressed Putrajaya for equitable treatment following the medical officer intake.
Addressing dental officers whose contracts ended without renewal, Dzulkefly maintained that MOH will keep monitoring their welfare and recognise their public service record.
During the same broadcast, Dzulkefly also expressed hope that the Treasury would clear a RM100 million seed grant to scale up non-communicable disease interventions across primary healthcare clinics nationwide.

Title: Hajiji: Sabah records strongest economic growth in six years
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Oct 14 — Sabah’s economy grew by 5.1 per cent last year, its strongest performance in six years, with gross domestic product (GDP) reaching RM88.8 billion, said Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor.
He said the growth was supported by the services sector, which expanded by 4.5 per cent, manufacturing (five per cent) and construction (28.3 per cent).
“Sabah has momentum. Our task now is to turn it into stronger local businesses, higher-value industries, better jobs and opportunities for communities across the state,” he said during his speech at the Sabah edition of Borneo 2026, which was delivered by Deputy Chief Minister II Datuk Seri Masidi Manjun.
Hajiji said the state’s record development ceiling of RM12.02 billion under the 13th Malaysia Plan, covering 933 new projects and 240 extension projects, would further strengthen Sabah’s competitiveness and attractiveness to investors.
Hajiji reiterated that Sabah has significant economic potential in agriculture, the Blue Economy and downstream industries, supported by its natural resources, biodiversity and strategic location.
The Blue Economy also offered considerable opportunities in modern fisheries, marine biotechnology and nature-based tourism, he said, adding that under SMJ 2.0, the sector had the potential to generate up to RM3.25 billion in additional income annually.
At a separate event, Hajiji said Sabah wanted to capture more economic value from its oil and gas resources by moving beyond exploration and production to downstream activities, technology, investment and the development of skilled local manpower.
He said the industry’s growth should create wider economic benefits for the state and its people, particularly by enabling Sabah-based companies and vendors to move beyond support services into higher-value activities requiring stronger technical, management and financial capabilities.
Hajiji said Petronas had an important role, alongside the state government, in creating opportunities for local companies to participate in larger segments of the industry’s value chain.
He said this during the signing ceremony of the land lease agreements for the Sabah Oil and Gas Terminal (SOGT) and Sabah-Sarawak Gas Pipeline (SSGP) projects between the Sabah Economic Development Corporation (SEDCO) and Petronas.
He also said the terminal (SOGT) and pipeline (SSGP) should be viewed not merely as operational infrastructure but as potential catalysts for further industrial and economic development, particularly along the Kimanis-Sipitang corridor.
He said the strategic location of these facilities could support further investment and industrial activities, adding that existing infrastructure should be leveraged to meet current needs while opening up future economic opportunities.
He said the land lease agreements signed between SEDCO and Petronas would provide greater certainty for the use of state land while safeguarding the state’s commercial interests. He expressed hope that the collaboration would evolve into a broader strategic partnership delivering lasting economic benefits to Sabah.

Title: Former e-hailing driver in JB gets eight years’ jail for making toddler eat faeces
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 —A former e-hailing driver was sentenced to eight years and six months’ imprisonment by the High Court in Johor Bahru today for abusing a three-year-old boy in 2022, which included forcing the child to eat his own excrement.
Chan Wen Jie, 32, pleaded guilty before Judicial Commissioner Datuk Abdul Fareed Abdul Gafoor to an alternative charge of child abuse under Section 31(1)(a) of the Child Act 2001,
FMT
reported.
The father of two was ordered to serve his sentence from his arrest on Oct 3, 2022, perform 36 hours of community service within six months, and execute a three-year good behaviour bond.
In his judgment, Fareed rejected the defence’s argument that the acts, captured on closed-circuit television, were merely intended to discipline the toddler.
“The accused not only caned the victim but also slapped him, hit him on the head and forced him to do squats, stand for long periods and eat his faeces from his disposable diaper.
“Forcing the child to eat faeces was a cruel and degrading act that could in no way be considered a form of discipline. If the accused was unable to care for the victim, he should have handed the child back to his father,” he said.
Chan was originally charged in 2022 with murdering the boy, Lee See Jie, at a house in Taman Skudai Ria, Skudai, on Oct 2.
The capital murder charge was subsequently withdrawn, with the court clarifying that it did not weigh the initial murder charge or the child’s cause of death when determining the sentence for the abuse offence.
Deputy Public Prosecutors Edelynn Wong and Nur Diyana Zubir prosecuted, while K. Sarawanakumar and Freda Sabapathy represented Chan.

Title: Tengku Zafrul: Malaysia should assess investors by job quality, treatment of women
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — Investors in Malaysia should be assessed on the quality of jobs they create and how they treat workers, particularly women, said Malaysian Investment Development Authority (Mida) chairman Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Abdul Aziz.
He said fair wages, safe workplaces and flexible working arrangements should be key criteria for quality investments.
“The investors we welcome to Malaysia should be judged by how they treat the women who work for them. Good jobs, fair pay, safe workplaces and flexible work.
“These are not favours. They are the new standard of a quality investment,” he said in his keynote address at the Annual Women Economic Forum and G100 Global Meet 2026 here today.
Citing McKinsey research, Tengku Zafrul said advancing women’s equality could add US$4.5 trillion (RM18.4 trillion) annually to Asia-Pacific economies, with Malaysia potentially gaining about US$50 billion a year, equivalent to roughly eight per cent of its gross domestic product.
He said greater workforce participation by women, alongside equal access to capital and markets for women entrepreneurs, would expand the economy’s productive capacity.
“When more women enter and remain in the workforce, women entrepreneurs have equal access to capital and markets, and talented women can rise into senior leadership, we expand the productive capacity of the entire economy.
“We enlarge the pool of ideas, skills and enterprise from which growth is created,” he said.
He noted that Malaysia’s female labour force participation rate reached a record 56.6 per cent at the end of 2025, but many women left the workforce after graduation because of inadequate childcare support and caregiving responsibilities.
He said women often had to balance their careers with caring for children and ageing parents, highlighting the need to address these barriers to enable more women to remain economically active.
Tengku Zafrul said empowering women was essential to unlocking Malaysia’s economic potential, particularly as countries competed for talent, productivity and innovation.
“In a world where every country is competing for talent, productivity and innovation, leaving women behind is not simply unjust, it is economically irrational,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia, Indonesia begin talks on joint action against forest fires causing haze, says Tok Mat
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 14 — Malaysia and Indonesia have begun discussions to explore ways of working together to tackle forest fires in Kalimantan and Sumatra that have caused transboundary haze.
Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said the discussions involved relevant agencies and ministries from both countries, including the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma), the Foreign Ministry and the National Security Council (MKN).
“Our secretary-general (Tan Sri Amran Mohamed Zin) has held discussions with MKN, Nadma and the Indonesian side on how we can jointly address these fires. This is the latest development.
“The form of cooperation will depend on the outcome of the discussions, but the authorities of both countries have, for the first time, begun talks on how we can work together to tackle the haze, which appears to be getting worse,” he said.
He was speaking to reporters after attending the handover ceremony for a solar photovoltaic (grid-connected PV) system installation project by the Works Ministry to the Foreign Ministry and three other government premises here today.
He said the discussions marked an initial step by both countries towards finding ways to cooperate in addressing forest fires and the haze, which had persisted for more than a month and was approaching two months.
Mohamad said the prolonged haze had affected not only Malaysia but also threatened the health of people in Indonesia and Singapore.
“Alhamdulillah, both countries, through their respective agencies and foreign ministries, will explore ways to cooperate and help address the forest fires together,” he said.
On Monday, Mohamad was reported as saying that Malaysia would raise the issue of transboundary haze at an Asean Foreign Ministers’ meeting ahead of the bloc’s 49th Summit in Manila next month, to discuss more effective regional mechanisms to tackle the problem. — Bernama

Title: Air quality deteriorates in 28 areas; Klang Valley, Johor hotspots rise
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — Air quality slipped further this afternoon, with 28 of the country's 68 monitoring stations recording unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 2pm, according to the Department of Environment (DOE).
The unhealthy tally rose from 27 this morning and 20 yesterday. Another 38 stations reported moderate air quality, while two recorded good levels.
Pasir Gudang in Johor logged the nation’s highest reading at 179, leading seven unhealthy stations in the state, including Pengerang (170), Kota Tinggi (168), and Larkin (166).
In the Klang Valley, Klang and peat fire hotspot Johan Setia tied at 175, while Cheras recorded 169, Putrajaya 166, Batu Muda 165, and both Shah Alam and Banting 162.
Elsewhere, Nilai in Negeri Sembilan held at 174, Port Dickson recorded 166, and Seremban stood at 161. All three Melaka stations were unhealthy, led by Bukit Rambai at 173.
On the east of the peninsula, Indera Mahkota in Pahang logged 156, alongside Kemaman (155) and Paka (153) in Terengganu.
In Sarawak, Sri Aman and IPD Serian eased to 126 and 125 respectively.
The persistent haze kept all schools closed today across Johor, Melaka, and Negeri Sembilan, alongside nine education districts in Selangor, Pahang, Sabah, and Sarawak.

Title: Children without citizenship eligible for school if one parent is Malaysian, says Sarawak minister
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 14 — Children who do not yet hold Malaysian citizenship remain eligible for access to education at government or government-aided schools if they have at least one biological parent who is a Malaysian citizen, subject to the conditions and procedures of the Education Ministry (MOE).
Sarawak Minister of Women, Childhood and Community Wellbeing Development Datuk Seri Fatimah Abdullah said this eligibility is governed by the Education Act 1996 (Act 550), the Education Regulations 1998 and MOE procedures currently in force.
“For the purpose of school admission, information on the biological parent who is a Malaysian citizen must be stated in the child’s birth certificate.
“Citizenship status and access to education are two separate matters,” she said during the question-and-answer session at the Sarawak State Legislative Assembly sitting here today.
She was responding to a question from Dr Johnichal Rayong Ngipa (GPS-Engkilili) on the status of children with a non-citizen parent but who were born and raised in Sarawak, as well as their eligibility to attend school.
Meanwhile, she said records from the National Registration Department (JPN) showed that 224 children born in Sarawak were registered as non-citizens between January and August this year.
“Among the main factors causing children to be registered as non-citizens or issued pink birth certificates are their parents’ marriages not registered or not recognised under Malaysian law.
“Other factors include mothers without valid identification documents, as well as cases of children who were found abandoned,” she said in reply to a supplementary question from Dr Rayong.
She said the state government is stepping up efforts to reduce the problem, including holding dialogues with communities and running awareness campaigns to encourage lawful marriage registration.
In addition, assistance will be given to mothers born in Sarawak but lacking identification documents to obtain such documents through the channels and procedures set out under the Sarawak Births and Deaths Registration Ordinance (Chapter 10). — Bernama

Title: King receives courtesy visit from Melaka governor ahead of Conference of Rulers meeting
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, today received a courtesy visit from Melaka Yang di-Pertua Negeri Tun Mohd Ali Mohd Rustam at Istana Negara in Kuala Lumpur.
The meeting took place before His Majesty attended the 273rd Conference of Rulers.
The 273rd Conference of Rulers is chaired by the Sultan of Perak, Sultan Nazrin Muizzuddin Shah.

Title: Thick smoke seen near DUKE Highway traced to burning streetlight
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — Thick smoke seen near the Duta-Ulu Kelang Expressway (DUKE), beyond the Sentul Toll Plaza on Wednesday, is believed to have been caused by a burning streetlight.
Sentul district police chief Assistant Commissioner Anuar Bakri Abdul Salam said inspections by police and DUKE highway management found that the smoke originated from a streetlight that had caught fire, according to a report by
Sinar Harian
.
“The fire was successfully extinguished and the incident did not involve any injuries or loss of life.
“Inspection findings showed that the smoke came from a burning streetlight and the fire was successfully extinguished,” he said in a statement on Wednesday.
A video showing thick smoke engulfing the area near the highway had earlier gone viral on social media.
The footage also showed several vehicles, including motorcycles, passing through the area.
Social media users had claimed that the smoke was coming from a drain near the highway, although its actual source had not been established at the time.
Anuar Bakri said the incident occurred at Ramp 0.5, along the route from Greenwood towards the exit leading to Kuala Lumpur Hospital (HKL).
He added that DUKE highway management was still handling follow-up action over the incident.

Title: Takiyuddin, Kiandee among four MPs appointed to Parliamentary Service Council
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — The Dewan Rakyat today approved a motion by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to appoint four lawmakers to the first Parliamentary Service Council established under the Parliamentary Service Act 2025.
The four lawmakers are Ramkarpal Singh (PH-Bukit Gelugor) and Datuk Seri Hasni Mohammad (BN-Simpang Renggam) from the government benches, and Datuk Seri Ronald Kiandee (PN-Beluran) and Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan (PN-Kota Bharu) from the Opposition.
The four were nominated by the Committee of Selection before the motion was tabled and approved by the Dewan Rakyat.
Under Section 3(2)(f) of the Parliamentary Service Act 2025, the power to nominate members rests with the Committee of Selection.
This is read together with Standing Order 76 of the Dewan Rakyat, which provides for the appointment of a Committee of Selection at the beginning of every Parliament.
The committee is bipartisan and chaired by the Speaker of the Dewan Rakyat.
The Anwar administration said the Parliamentary Service Act 2025 (Act 869) was intended to fulfil “a long-standing demand for institutional reform” and restore structural independence to Malaysia’s legislative branch.
The Act, according to government leaders, would make Parliamentary services independent from the public service that is mainly under executive control, with the Parliamentary Service Council given autonomy to manage internal administration, human resources, and finances.
The Act reverses a 33-year arrangement under which Parliament’s administration, staffing and budget fell under the direct jurisdiction of the Prime Minister’s Department.
The Parliamentary Service Council also comprises ex-officio members, including the Director-General of Public Service, the Treasury Secretary-General, the Chief Administrator of Parliament, the Attorney General or their designated representative, and the clerks of both the Dewan Rakyat and Dewan Negara.
